_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with tardive dyskinesia

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel, fixed-dose study of valbenazine 40 mg/day, 80 mg/day, or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe tardive dyskinesia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to end of Week 6 in Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale (AIMS) total dyskinesia score
pivotal_trials.n: 234 subjects randomized (primary analysis: placebo N=76, 40 mg N=70, 80 mg N=79)
pivotal_trials.result: Valbenazine 80 mg/day significantly superior to placebo: AIMS LS mean difference vs placebo -3.1 (95% CI -4.2, -2.0), p<0.0001; 40 mg difference -1.8 (95% CI -3.0, -0.7), p=0.002

key_safety: Most common adverse reaction (>=5% and twice placebo): somnolence (10.9% vs 4.2% placebo). Other reactions included anticholinergic effects (5.4% vs 4.9%), balance disorders/fall (4.1% vs 2.2%), and akathisia (2.7% vs 0.5%). QT prolongation is a warning.
target_moa: Valbenazine is a vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) inhibitor; it and its active metabolite [+]-alpha-dihydrotetrabenazine cause reversible reduction of dopamine release at presynaptic nerve terminals
modality: Small molecule (VMAT2 inhibitor; new molecular entity)

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues

basis.text: Priority review designated by the Division because there are no approved treatments for TD and Breakthrough status was granted

citations.quote: Review of this drug was designated priority by the Division because there are no approved treatments for TD, and Breakthrough Status was granted.

summary.text: INGREZZA (valbenazine), a new molecular entity, received Fast Track (2012), Breakthrough Therapy (2014), and priority review, and was approved on the original review cycle as the first FDA-approved treatment for tardive dyskinesia; it was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: The Applicant applied for Fast Track designation on November 22, 2011, which was granted on January 24, 2012.

Valbenazine was granted designation as a Breakthrough Therapy in October, 2014, based on the Division's view that the drug is intended to treat a serious condition, and that preliminary evidence indicated it may provide substantial improvement over currently available therapies (there were none). Priority review was also granted.
Because there are no currently-approved treatments for TD, valbenazine will represent the first treatment option for this unmet medical need.
